country.name: Brasil
country.languagePolicy: Brazilian Portuguese is the default interface language. Libras and Indigenous languages require appropriate bilingual, community and institutional review; automatic translation is not reviewed localization.

review.policy: No category becomes verified without a named qualified Brazilian reviewer, current authoritative sources and review of the responsible federal, state, Federal District, municipal, community, institution or course authority.

governanceModel.summary: Brazil's education system operates through collaboration among the Union, states, Federal District and municipalities. MEC provides national policy and regulation, CNE issues national norms, INEP maintains education statistics and evaluations, subnational systems govern applicable basic-education operations, and e-MEC records higher-education institutions, courses and authorizing acts.
governanceModel.schoolDataAuthority: Instituto Nacional de Estudos e Pesquisas Educacionais Anísio Teixeira (INEP)
governanceModel.schoolRule: Preserve INEP school code, administrative dependency, category, education stages and modalities, municipality, state, operating status, Census reference year and review date.
governanceModel.higherEducationRule: Institutional accreditation or re-accreditation, course authorization, recognition or renewal of recognition, delivery address or modality, and SINAES quality indicators are distinct records and claims.

authorities.name: Ministério da Educação
authorities.role: national education policy and federal higher-education regulation and supervision

authorities.name: Conselho Nacional de Educação
authorities.role: national education norms and curricular resolutions

authorities.name: Instituto Nacional de Estudos e Pesquisas Educacionais Anísio Teixeira
authorities.role: Censo Escolar, school catalog, higher-education census, assessment and quality indicators

authorities.name: State, Federal District and municipal education systems
authorities.role: subnational curricula, school authorization and administration within their legal competence

authorities.name: Cadastro e-MEC
authorities.role: official registry of higher-education institutions, courses, authorizing acts and evaluation information

authorities.name: Autoridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados
Conselhos Tutelares and the child-protection system
authorities.role: local protection of children and adolescents under the ECA

curriculum.title: Base Nacional Comum Curricular and current CNE curricular norms
curriculum.implementationRule: Confirm stage, area or component, BNCC version, current CNE norms, the relevant state or municipal curriculum and the school's Projeto Político-Pedagógico before mapping a resource.
curriculum.supplementPolicy: External materials may supplement but never silently replace the BNCC, current CNE rules, the applicable subnational curriculum, the school's pedagogical plan, or an Indigenous, Quilombola or bilingual community-governed curriculum.

schoolDirectory.authority: INEP, with school declarations and collaboration from state, Federal District and municipal education administrations
schoolDirectory.scopeNotice: The catalog uses annually updated Censo Escolar declarations and includes active or paused public and private basic-education schools. A catalog record does not by itself prove current authorization for every stage, modality, site or service.

educationStatistics.scopeNotice: Every figure must display Census reference year, publication date, measure, population, geography, administrative dependency, source and filters. Declaratory administrative data and evaluation indicators must not be combined or presented as current without labeling.

higherEducation.regulatoryAuthority: MEC, with CNE and INEP functions as applicable
higherEducation.registryName: Cadastro Nacional de Cursos e Instituições de Educação Superior — Cadastro e-MEC
higherEducation.authorityNotice: Institutional accreditation or re-accreditation, course authorization, recognition or renewal of recognition, delivery address and modality, regulatory process status, and SINAES evaluation indicators are distinct. Each claim must identify the institution or course code, act, scope, date and current status.

privacyAndSafeguarding.dataProtectionLaw: Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados Pessoais — Lei nº 13.709/2018, as amended
privacyAndSafeguarding.childrenLaw: Estatuto da Criança e do Adolescente — Lei nº 8.069/1990, compiled text
privacyAndSafeguarding.scopeNotice: LGPD legal bases, the best interests of children and adolescents, parental or guardian involvement where applicable, ECA safeguards, incident handling and institutional protocols require qualified Brazilian review before real learner participation.

culturalAndLanguageRequirements.rule: Indigenous and Quilombola curricula require participation by the relevant communities and competent education systems. Education for signing deaf learners must respect Libras as the language of instruction and written Portuguese as the second language where the bilingual modality applies. BRASA must not substitute automatic translation for these processes.

completionCriteria: A qualified Brazilian education reviewer is named.
Federal, state, Federal District and municipal responsibilities are reviewed for the participating jurisdiction.
Every school record preserves INEP code, administrative dependency, stages, modalities, status, Census reference year and review date.
Every statistic shows reference year, publication date, definition, geography, population and provenance.
Every higher-education claim distinguishes institutional accreditation, course authorization or recognition, location, modality, regulatory status and quality indicators.
Curriculum mappings identify stage, area or component, BNCC version, current CNE norm, applicable subnational curriculum and school pedagogical plan.
Indigenous, Quilombola and Libras education requirements are reviewed with competent community participation.
Current LGPD, ANPD child-data guidance, ECA requirements and local safeguarding protocols are reviewed by qualified Brazilian counsel.
Privacy, safeguarding, accessibility, incident and consent procedures are approved by each participating institution.
No authorization, recognition, accreditation, partnership or credential claim exceeds documentary evidence.
